title: Object.keys values and entries Check
description: Turn objects into key/value/entry lists for iteration.

questions.explanation: These methods skip the prototype chain and non-enumerable / Symbol keys (for the usual string-key case).

questions.prompt: Given a prototype property `inherited` and own `own`, what does `Object.keys(obj)` return?
questions.explanation: `in` would see inherited keys; `Object.keys` does not.

questions.prompt: Does mutating the array returned by `Object.keys(obj)` change `obj`?

options.text: No — you get a new array

questions.explanation: The result is a fresh array. Changing it does not rename or remove object properties.

questions.prompt: Which loop pattern pairs naturally with `Object.entries`?

options.text: `for (const key of Object.entries(obj))` where key is a string

questions.explanation: Each entry is a two-element array, so destructuring `[key, value]` is the usual form.
